- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early periods of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias in the first 5–10 days, then plateau or slightly decline — true values often rise faster or overshoot initially.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+), model tends to overcorrect or underestimate the subsequent rebound — true values often show a stronger recovery or sustained higher levels.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the short term — true values frequently revert to historical averages faster than forecasted.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 1–3 days in most cases, especially after volatility spikes.
- Model overestimates downward trends in low-price regimes (e.g., 60–70 range) — true values often stabilize or rebound faster.
- In high volatility periods, model underreacts to news or policy changes — true values show sharper directional shifts than forecasted.
